title: ci(test-ui): two nits from #31962 — planner header density claim, wiring-test filter stand-in
body:
domain:devx#2 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTo666XXx9e1Gm21C6

Filing gate: ② two nits a contract review graded on #31962 (record 6745712800), accepted there as deviations so the head did not move (ACCEPT 6745741064). ⛔ Not a claim.

## Problem

1. **Header claim not by construction (record F1).** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `test-ui-plan` header says the plan keeps "no planned leg denser than a full-battery leg". The bins (slots 2..N+1) are bounded by D by construction; the always-on lane on slot 1 is not. Today the lane predicts 1,731 of D = 1,856 predicted-s, so the sentence is true now and would silently go false as the always-on set grows.
2. **Wiring-test stand-in (record F2).** `ui/scripts/__tests__/select-affected-tests-wiring.test.ts` asserts slot 1's argv equals the lane and that the union of argv files equals the selection. Since `plan-test-ui-shards.mjs files` emits only a filter unit's shortest path, a future substring pair (`x.test.ts` / `x.test.tsx`) would red this test though the leg is correct (fail-red, test-only; 0 such pairs among the 6,715 ui test paths at `66268cce`). Its filter stand-in also matches case-sensitively, while vitest's filename filter is case-insensitive.

## Ask

- Reword the header to what holds by construction (bins ≤ D; the lane is whatever the always-on set predicts), or have the planner warn or refuse when the lane's predicted seconds exceed D, whichever the seat rules.
- Make the wiring test expand a unit's shortest path back to its members (as vitest would, case-insensitively) before comparing, with one fixture pair that pins it.
- ⛔ No test skipped or dropped, no change to what a leg runs.

## Done when

The header sentence is true by construction, and the wiring test passes on a fixture with a `x.test.ts` / `x.test.tsx` pair and a case-only difference.

## Reader

`domain:devx`, from triage. Related: #31914 (closed by #31962), #31939 (PR 1).
